name: Com hen
summary: Rice with tiny Perfume River clams, herbs, bean sprouts, peanuts, and pork rind. The plate is on Hen Island.
origin: Hue. Vietnam Tourism calls it a peasant plate built on leftover rice.
history: Vietnam Tourism traces cơm hến to a peasant kitchen: leftover rice and baby clams from the Perfume River. The same dish is also described as cold rice. Vietnam Tourism does not name a utensil.
culture: On that same page it sits opposite the court dishes. It is the plate of the river island, not a banquet course.
texture: The plate is rice with baby clams, bean sprouts, and strips of pork rind.
taste: The plate carries shrimp paste, roasted peanuts, herbs, bean sprouts, and pork rind. Mix the rice with the clams, the herbs, and the shrimp paste.
howToEat: Cross Ưng Bình bridge to Hen Island. The walk is under half an hour. Vietnam Tourism says the island disappears when the city floods, so skip it in a flood week.
where: Hen Island, Cồn Hến. Chi Lăng and Bạch Đằng are the afternoon streets on the far side. The hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Com hen in Hue — rice and clams on Hen Island
seoDescription: Rice with tiny river clams, herbs, peanuts, and pork rind. Cross Ung Binh bridge to Hen Island. The island floods. A stall price is Check on arrival.
